Player Recruitment & Similarity Scouting Tool¶

Anthony Adusei-Poku · MSc Data Science, University of East London (2025)

Question a club analyst gets asked: "Find me someone who plays like player X, but is cheaper or younger."

This notebook builds position-aware per-90 player profiles from StatsBomb 2015/16 event data (big-five leagues), links every player to Transfermarkt market values and dates of birth (CC0 transfermarkt-datasets), and then:

  1. validates the similarity measure with a split-half re-identification test,
  2. clusters players into data-driven roles,
  3. works through three real recruitment briefs from the summer 2016 transfer window, and
  4. back-tests whether the tool's cheap "lookalikes" went on to rise in value.

Data recreation: python src/download_statsbomb.py && python src/download_transfermarkt.py && python src/link_transfermarkt.py.

2. Player profiles¶

One profile per outfield player for the season (all clubs combined), minimum 900 minutes (10 full matches). Each player is assigned to the position group where he played most minutes. Defensive volumes are possession-adjusted (PAdj) match by match: a count is multiplied by 0.5 / (opponent's share of passes), so a defender at a dominant side like Barcelona is not penalised for having fewer chances to defend. Percentages are shrunk towards the league-wide rate with 10 pseudo-attempts so that small samples do not produce extreme values.

def leaders(col, group=None, n=5):
    d = prof if group is None else prof[prof.group == group]
    return d.nlargest(n, col)[["display_name", "team", col]].reset_index(drop=True)

3. Similarity method and validation¶

Each feature is converted to a z-score within the player's position group (so a centre-back's passing is judged against other centre-backs), and similarity is the cosine similarity between two players' z-score vectors (1 = identical style, 0 = unrelated, negative = opposite).

Validation: split-half re-identification. If a profile captures a player's genuine style, a player's profile from one half of his matches should be most similar to his own profile from the other half. Each player's appearances are split alternately into two halves (≥450 minutes in each), and for every player I rank all players in the same position group from the other half. A random guess would find the right player first about 0.4% of the time.

In [7]:
pm_sorted = pm.sort_values("match_date").copy()
pm_sorted["half"] = pm_sorted.groupby("player_id").cumcount() % 2
A = sc.build_profiles(450, pm_sorted[pm_sorted.half == 0]).set_index("player_id")
B = sc.build_profiles(450, pm_sorted[pm_sorted.half == 1]).set_index("player_id")
ids = A.index.intersection(B.index).intersection(prof.index)
A, B = A.loc[ids].copy(), B.loc[ids].copy()
A["group"] = B["group"] = prof.loc[ids, "group"]
RAW = {f: f.replace("_padj", "") for f in sc.FEATURE_COLS if "_padj" in f}

def reidentify(feats, by_group=True, metric="cosine", pca=None):
    ranks, pool = [], []
    allab = pd.concat([A[feats], B[feats]]).astype(float)
    for g in A.group.unique():
        a, b = A.loc[A.group == g, feats].astype(float), B.loc[B.group == g, feats].astype(float)
        ref = pd.concat([a, b]) if by_group else allab
        mu, sd = ref.mean(), ref.std(ddof=0)
        za, zb = ((a - mu) / sd).values, ((b - mu) / sd).values
        if pca:
            p = PCA(pca, random_state=0).fit(np.vstack([za, zb])); za, zb = p.transform(za), p.transform(zb)
        if metric == "cosine":
            S = (za / np.linalg.norm(za, axis=1, keepdims=True)) @ (zb / np.linalg.norm(zb, axis=1, keepdims=True)).T
        else:
            S = -((za[:, None, :] - zb[None, :, :]) ** 2).sum(-1)
        ranks += list((S > np.diag(S)[:, None]).sum(1) + 1); pool += [len(a)] * len(a)
    r = np.array(ranks)
    return {"top-1": (r == 1).mean(), "top-5": (r <= 5).mean(), "median rank": np.median(r),
            "chance top-1": np.mean(1 / np.array(pool))}

methods = {
    "Cosine, z within position (chosen)": dict(feats=sc.FEATURE_COLS),
    "Euclidean, z within position": dict(feats=sc.FEATURE_COLS, metric="euclidean"),
    "Cosine on PCA (90% variance)": dict(feats=sc.FEATURE_COLS, pca=0.9),
    "Cosine, z across all outfield players": dict(feats=sc.FEATURE_COLS, by_group=False),
    "Cosine, no possession adjustment": dict(feats=[RAW.get(f, f) for f in sc.FEATURE_COLS]),
}
val = pd.DataFrame({k: reidentify(**v) for k, v in methods.items()}).T
print(f"{len(ids):,} players with 450+ minutes in both halves")
val

# How often is the best match a team-mate? (team style can leak into individual profiles)
Z = sc.standardise(prof)
U = Z.values / np.linalg.norm(Z.values, axis=1, keepdims=True)
S = U @ U.T
np.fill_diagonal(S, -np.inf)
g_arr = prof.group.to_numpy(str); t_arr = prof.team.to_numpy(str)
same_group = g_arr[:, None] == g_arr[None, :]
S_g = np.where(same_group, S, -np.inf)
best = S_g.argmax(1)
teammate = (t_arr[best] == t_arr).mean()
exp_teammate = np.mean([((prof.group == g) & (prof.team == t)).sum() - 1 for g, t in zip(prof.group, prof.team)] /
                       (prof.group.map(prof.group.value_counts()) - 1))
print(f"Best same-position match is a team-mate for {teammate:.1%} of players (random expectation {exp_teammate:.1%})")
print(f"Median best-match similarity: {np.median(S_g.max(1)):.3f}")

4. Data-driven player roles¶

Positions on a team sheet hide very different jobs: a ball-playing centre-back and an aerial stopper both appear as "CB". To find roles, all outfield players are standardised together, reduced with PCA (components explaining 90% of variance) and clustered with k-means. Silhouette scores are low for every k (player styles form a continuum rather than clean groups), so k = 9 was chosen for interpretability: it is the smallest k that separates the two centre-back types. Clusters are named after inspecting their average profiles; each name is pinned to an anchor player so the labels are reproducible.

In [10]:
Zall = sc.standardise(prof, by_group=False)
pca = PCA(0.9, random_state=0).fit(Zall)
Xp = pca.transform(Zall)
print(f"PCA: {pca.n_components_} components explain {pca.explained_variance_ratio_.sum():.1%} of variance")
sil = {k: silhouette_score(Xp, KMeans(k, n_init=20, random_state=0).fit_predict(Xp)) for k in range(4, 13)}
print("Silhouette by k:", {k: round(v, 3) for k, v in sil.items()})
km = KMeans(9, n_init=50, random_state=0).fit(Xp)
prof["cluster"] = km.labels_
ANCHORS = {"Ball-playing centre-back": "Martín Demichelis", "Stopper centre-back": "Ryan Shawcross",
           "Attacking full-back": "Joel Ward", "Ball-winning midfielder": "Victor Wanyama",
           "Deep-lying playmaker": "Luca Cigarini", "Pressing box-to-box midfielder": "Marco Benassi",
           "Creative playmaker": "Christian Eriksen", "Dribbling winger": "Iñaki Williams",
           "Penalty-box striker": "Salomón Rondón"}
name_of = {prof.loc[prof.display_name == a, "cluster"].iloc[0]: r for r, a in ANCHORS.items()}
assert len(name_of) == 9, "anchor players must fall in different clusters"
prof["role"] = prof.cluster.map(name_of)
print(f"Silhouette at k=9: {sil[9]:.3f}")

Zpos = sc.standardise(prof)  # z-scores relative to each player's position group
ROLE_ORDER = ["Stopper centre-back", "Ball-playing centre-back", "Attacking full-back", "Ball-winning midfielder",
              "Deep-lying playmaker", "Pressing box-to-box midfielder", "Creative playmaker", "Dribbling winger",
              "Penalty-box striker"]
rows = []
for r in ROLE_ORDER:
    d = prof[prof.role == r]
    z = Zpos.loc[d.index].mean().sort_values(ascending=False)
    ex = d.nlargest(5, "minutes").display_name.tolist()
    rows.append({"role": r, "players": len(d),
                 "main positions": ", ".join(f"{g} {n}" for g, n in d.group.value_counts().head(2).items()),
                 "strongest traits vs position peers": ", ".join(sc.FEATURES[c][0] for c in z.index[:3]),
                 "examples (most minutes)": ", ".join(ex)})
roles = pd.DataFrame(rows).set_index("role")
roles.to_csv("results/role_clusters.csv")

5. The scouting tool¶

find_similar(prof, player, max_value=None, max_age=None, leagues=None) in src/scouting.py returns the most similar players in the same position group, filtered by Transfermarkt value at 1 July 2016 (the opening of the summer window), age and league. It also runs from the command line:

python src/scouting.py "Kanté" --max-value 10 --max-age 26
In [14]:

           "tackles_padj_90", "interceptions_padj_90", "blocks_padj_90", "clearances_padj_90", "pressures_padj_90",
           "aerials_won_90", "aerial_pct", "def_height"],
    "ST": ["npxg_90", "shots_90", "xg_per_shot", "box_receipts_90", "xa_90", "key_passes_90", "dribbles_90",
           "dribble_pct", "prog_carries_90", "passes_90", "turnovers_90", "pressures_att3_90", "aerials_won_90", "aerial_pct"],
    "AM/W": ["npxg_90", "shots_90", "xa_90", "key_passes_90", "passes_into_box_90", "crosses_90", "through_balls_90",
             "prog_passes_90", "prog_carries_90", "dribbles_90", "dribble_pct", "turnovers_90", "pressures_att3_90",
             "recoveries_padj_90"],
    "FB": ["crosses_90", "xa_90", "passes_into_box_90", "prog_passes_90", "prog_carries_90", "dribbles_90", "pass_pct",
           "tackles_padj_90", "interceptions_padj_90", "pressures_padj_90", "recoveries_padj_90", "blocks_padj_90",
           "aerial_pct", "def_height"],
}

def percentiles(i):
    g = P.loc[i, "group"]
    peers = P[P.group == g]
    out = {}
    for c in RADAR[g]:
        pct = (peers[c] < P.loc[i, c]).mean() * 100 + (peers[c] == P.loc[i, c]).mean() * 50
        out[c] = 100 - pct if c in sc.LOWER_IS_BETTER else pct
    return out

def radar_compare(target, matches, fname, title):
    ti = sc.lookup(P, target)
    g = P.loc[ti, "group"]
    params = [sc.FEATURES[c][0] + (" (inv.)" if c in sc.LOWER_IS_BETTER else "") for c in RADAR[g]]
    radar = Radar(params, [0] * len(params), [100] * len(params), round_int=[True] * len(params),
                  num_rings=4, ring_width=1, center_circle_radius=1)
    fig, axs = plt.subplots(1, len(matches), figsize=(7.4 * len(matches), 8))
    tv = list(percentiles(ti).values())
    for ax, (mi, sim) in zip(np.atleast_1d(axs), matches):
        radar.setup_axis(ax=ax)
        radar.draw_circles(ax=ax, facecolor="#f3f3f3", edgecolor="#d0d0d0")
        mv = list(percentiles(mi).values())
        _, _, vt, vm = radar.draw_radar_compare(tv, mv, ax=ax, kwargs_radar={"facecolor": "#1f4e79", "alpha": 0.55},
                                               kwargs_compare={"facecolor": "#f39c12", "alpha": 0.55})
        radar.draw_param_labels(ax=ax, fontsize=10.5)
        r = P.loc[mi]
        val = f"€{r.value_m:.1f}m" if pd.notna(r.value_m) else "value n/a"
        ax.set_title(f"{r.display_name} ({r.team})\nage {r.age:.0f} · {val} · similarity {sim:.2f}",
                     color="#b9770e", fontsize=12, fontweight="bold", pad=18)
    t = P.loc[ti]
    fig.suptitle(f"{title}\nBlue: {t.display_name} ({t.team}, age {t.age:.0f}, €{t.value_m:.0f}m) · percentile vs "
                 f"{sc.GROUP_LABEL[g].lower()}s, big-five leagues 2015/16 (rings = 25th/50th/75th/100th)", fontsize=13.5, fontweight="bold", y=1.02)
    plt.savefig(FIG + fname); plt.show()

def bargain_map(target, max_value, max_age, fname, n_label=6):
    ti = sc.lookup(P, target); t = P.loc[ti]
    U = Zp.values / np.linalg.norm(Zp.values, axis=1, keepdims=True)
    sim = U @ U[ti]
    d = P.assign(similarity=sim)
    d = d[(d.group == t.group) & (d.index != ti) & d.value_m.notna()]
    ok = (d.value_2016_eur <= max_value) & (d.age < max_age + 1)
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9.5, 5.6))
    ax.scatter(d.loc[~ok, "value_m"], d.loc[~ok, "similarity"], s=16, color="#c8c8c8", label="outside brief")
    ax.scatter(d.loc[ok, "value_m"], d.loc[ok, "similarity"], s=26, color="#f39c12", label=f"meets brief (≤ €{max_value/1e6:.0f}m, age ≤ {max_age})")
    lab = pd.concat([d[ok].nlargest(n_label, "similarity"), d[~ok].nlargest(2, "similarity")])
    texts = [ax.text(r.value_m, r.similarity, f"{r.display_name} ({r.similarity:.2f})", fontsize=8.5) for _, r in lab.iterrows()]
    adjust_text(texts, ax=ax, arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="-", color="#666666", lw=0.6))
    ax.set_xscale("log"); ax.axvline(max_value / 1e6, color="#f39c12", ls="--", lw=1)
    ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(plt.FuncFormatter(lambda v, _: f"€{v:g}m"))
    ax.set_xlabel("Transfermarkt value at 1 July 2016 (€m, log scale)"); ax.set_ylabel(f"Cosine similarity to {t.display_name}")
    ax.set_title(f"Bargain map: who plays like {t.display_name}? ({sc.GROUP_LABEL[t.group].lower()}s)", loc="left", fontweight="bold")
    from matplotlib.lines import Line2D
    h = [Line2D([], [], marker="o", ls="", color="#f39c12", label=f"meets brief (≤ €{max_value/1e6:.0f}m, age ≤ {max_age})"),
         Line2D([], [], marker="o", ls="", color="#c8c8c8", label="outside brief")]
    ax.legend(handles=h, frameon=False, loc="lower left"); plt.savefig(FIG + fname); plt.show()

def summer_moves(names, start="2016-06-01", end="2017-09-01"):
    ids = P.set_index("display_name").loc[names, "tm_player_id"].dropna().astype(int)
    t = transfers[transfers.player_id.isin(ids) & transfers.transfer_date.between(start, end)
                  & (transfers.from_club_name != transfers.to_club_name)]
    t = t[~((t.transfer_date.dt.month == 6) & (t.transfer_date.dt.day == 30))]  # end-of-loan returns
    t = t[~t.to_club_name.str.contains("U19|U21|U23|B$|Retired|Without Club", regex=True, na=False)]
    return t[["player_name", "transfer_date", "from_club_name", "to_club_name", "transfer_fee"]].assign(
        transfer_fee=lambda x: (x.transfer_fee / 1e6).round(1)).rename(columns={"transfer_fee": "fee_€m"}).sort_values("transfer_date")

def show(res):
    res = res.copy()
    res["value_m"] = res.value_m.map(lambda v: f"€{v:.1f}m" if pd.notna(v) else "n/a")
    res["age"] = res.age.round(0).astype("Int64"); res["minutes"] = res.minutes.round(0).astype(int)
    return res.reset_index(drop=True)

6. Back-test: did the cheap lookalikes rise in value?¶

A tool like this is only useful if it surfaces players the market undervalues. For every target valued at €25m+ in summer 2016, I take the five most similar same-position players valued at ≤ ⅓ of the target and aged ≤ 24, and compare their Transfermarkt value change to July 2018 with every other player who met the same brief (same position group, same value cap and age limit). Values are Transfermarkt crowd estimates, so this is a test against market opinion, not of on-pitch success.

In [22]:
U = Zp.values / np.linalg.norm(Zp.values, axis=1, keepdims=True)
P["log_change"] = np.log(P.value_2018_eur / P.value_2016_eur)
targets = P[P.value_2016_eur >= 25e6]
bt, pools, picked = [], set(), set()
for ti, t in targets.iterrows():
    sim = U @ U[ti]
    elig = P[(P.group == t.group) & (P.index != ti) & (P.value_2016_eur <= t.value_2016_eur / 3) & (P.age < 25)
             & P.log_change.notna()].assign(similarity=lambda d: sim[d.index])
    if len(elig) < 15:
        continue
    top = elig.nlargest(5, "similarity")
    market = elig.nlargest(5, "value_2016_eur")   # naive baseline: the five most expensive players who fit the brief
    rest = elig.drop(top.index)
    pools |= set(elig.index); picked |= set(top.index)
    bt.append({"target": t.display_name, "group": t.group, "pool": len(elig),
               "top5_median_change": np.exp(top.log_change.median()) - 1,
               "pool_median_change": np.exp(rest.log_change.median()) - 1,
               "top5_mean_log": top.log_change.mean(), "rest_mean_log": rest.log_change.mean(),
               "market5_mean_log": market.log_change.mean()})
bt = pd.DataFrame(bt)
bt["diff_log"] = bt.top5_mean_log - bt.rest_mean_log
print(f"{len(bt)} targets valued ≥ €25m with ≥15 eligible players; {len(picked)} different players appear in the top-5 lists")
print(f"Top-5 lookalikes rose more (mean log change) than the rest of the pool for {(bt.diff_log > 0).mean():.1%} of targets, "
      f"and more than the five most expensive eligible players for {(bt.top5_mean_log > bt.market5_mean_log).mean():.1%}")
print(f"Average over targets, value multiple 2016→2018: top 5 ×{np.exp(bt.top5_mean_log.mean()):.2f}, "
      f"rest of pool ×{np.exp(bt.rest_mean_log.mean()):.2f}, five most expensive ×{np.exp(bt.market5_mean_log.mean()):.2f}")

85 targets valued ≥ €25m with ≥15 eligible players; 156 different players appear in the top-5 lists
Top-5 lookalikes rose more (mean log change) than the rest of the pool for 71.8% of targets, and more than the five most expensive eligible players for 81.2%
Average over targets, value multiple 2016→2018: top 5 ×1.92, rest of pool ×1.52, five most expensive ×1.43

The same players are recommended for several targets, so targets are not independent. A stricter test counts each player once: every player who was eligible for at least one brief is either picked (in some top-5 list) or never picked, and I compare their value change while controlling for starting value, age and minutes played.

In [23]:
u = P.loc[sorted(pools)].assign(picked=lambda d: d.index.isin(picked))
from scipy.stats import mannwhitneyu
mw = mannwhitneyu(u.loc[u.picked, "log_change"], u.loc[~u.picked, "log_change"], alternative="greater")
summary = u.groupby("picked").agg(players=("log_change", "size"), median_value_2016_m=("value_m", "median"),
                                  median_age=("age", "median"), median_value_change=("log_change", lambda x: np.exp(x.median()) - 1))
display(summary)
print(f"Mann-Whitney U (picked > never picked): p = {mw.pvalue:.2g}")
X = np.column_stack([np.ones(len(u)), u.picked.astype(float), np.log(u.value_2016_eur), u.age, np.log(u.minutes)])
y = u.log_change.values
coef = np.linalg.lstsq(X, y, rcond=None)[0]
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
bs = [np.linalg.lstsq(X[i], y[i], rcond=None)[0][1] for i in (rng.integers(0, len(u), len(u)) for _ in range(2000))]
lo, hi = np.percentile(bs, [2.5, 97.5])
print(f"OLS log value change ~ picked + log value + age + log minutes ({len(u)} players): "
      f"picked coefficient {coef[1]:+.3f} (×{np.exp(coef[1]):.2f}; 95% bootstrap CI {lo:+.3f} to {hi:+.3f})")
backtest_stats = {"picked_coef": coef[1], "ci_lo": lo, "ci_hi": hi, "mw_p": mw.pvalue, "n_players": len(u), "n_picked": len(picked)}
